title: Zero-to-release SDK onramp — sprint log & quickstart sketch
content:
Purpose
----
This doc is a working sprint-log + quickstart sketch to take a minimal SDK onramp from prototype -> public docs -> release. Focus: 0 to a reproducible first-run for engineers who want to embed Redwood inference into an app in under 10 minutes. Keep optics on: time-to-first-success, surface failure modes, telemetry needed for observability, and clear rollback/compat constraints.

High-level goals (MVP)
- 3-minute path for a JS dev (npm install, env set, run).
- Example app: TODO list assistant (minimal server + client) that calls the hosted API and streams responses.
- Telemetry baked in: first-success, sdk-init, call-latency, fallback-used, cache-hit.
- Public quickstart + downloadables (zip sample app, curl snippet, minimal Dockerfile).

Sprint summary (high-level log)
- 2026-01-08: Kickoff. Decided minimal language: JS/TS first, Python later. Owner: Maya. Outcome: prototype sample app by end of week.
- 2026-01-15: Prototype sample app (server+client) with streaming working. Owner: Omar. Note: missing ergonomic retry behavior; basic exponential backoff added.
- 2026-01-22: Telemetry events defined and proto-instrumented. Owner: Sofia. Open: event schema review (RDW-1024).
- 2026-02-02: Internal alpha test with 5 engineers. Feedback: env var density too high; onboarding too many steps.
- 2026-02-18: Reduced env vars, added 'redwood run-demo' convenience script. Owner: Liam.
- 2026-02-28: Smoke tests & CI pipeline for quickstart artifacts. Owner: Maya. CI flake observed on matrix node 14.x.
- 2026-03-05: Draft copy for public quickstart page. Owner: content + Maya.

Quickstart outline (text for landing page / README)
1) Install + create project
   - npm init my-app && cd my-app
   - npm install @redwood-inference/sdk
2) Configure credentials (minimal)
   - export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx  # or use .env
   - optional: export REDWOOD_REGION=us-east-1
3) Run the demo (server streams response)
   - npx redwood-sdk start-demo
   - Expected: browser UI shows streaming tokens, first suggestion appears ~400ms; check telemetry: sdk-init and first-success events fired in dashboard.

Sample curl & minimal JS usage (to copy/paste into README)
- curl example:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-mini","prompt":"Suggest a 3-step plan to write a README","max_tokens":80}'

- JS snippet (node)
  const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood-inference/sdk');
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
  const stream = client.generateStream({ model: 'redwood-mini', prompt: 'Write a TODO' });
  stream.on('token', t => process.stdout.write(t));
  stream.on('done', () => console.log('\ncomplete'));

Developer experience priorities (decisions & constraints)
- Minimize required configuration: only API key required for hosted path. Region and telemetry toggles optional.
- Provide sane defaults for timeouts (15s for first token, 60s total) and backoff.
- Local dev: provide a hermetic `--local` mode that stubs responses for offline demos.
- Keep the SDK surface tiny: generate, embed, embeddings, health-check. Avoid exposing routing policies in v1 of SDK.

Telemetry & observability (list of events we must emit)
- sdk.init (sdk version, platform, env)
- sdk.first_success (time_to_first_token_ms, model)
- sdk.request.sent (request_id, model, mode: sync/stream)
- sdk.request.fallback (fallback_model, reason)
- sdk.cache.hit (key, ttl)
- sdk.error (error_code, message)
Notes: keep PII out of payloads. All event payload fields need schema approval (RDW-1024).

Acceptance criteria for public quickstart (must all pass)
- A fresh macOS dev with Node 18+ can follow README and reach 'first token' in under 10 minutes.
- CI has reproducible smoke test that runs sample app and verifies telemetry events were emitted.
- README contains explicit troubleshooting section with 3 common failures and one-line fixes.
- Downloadable sample zip < 2MB gzipped and builds in CI container.

Smoke checklist (to add as GitHub actions job)
- node versions: 18, 20 matrix
- env rule: missing API key -> clear error message
- streaming: verifies tokens arrive (use a token count > 3)
- telemetry: mock endpoint receives sdk.init and first_success within 30s

Edge cases & unresolved questions
- Q: Auth flows for enterprise (SSO / token rotation). Plan: call out enterprise primer and link to private deployment docs; defer for v1.
- Q: Should SDK auto-retry with fallback model if quota hit? Risk: surprising cost. Proposal: opt-in via config.fallback = true.
- Q: How opinionated should local stubs be? Need to avoid tests that diverge from hosted behavior. Suggest we keep stubs minimal and surface a stub-verifier test helper.

Rollout & release plan (minimal)
- Cut v0.1.0-beta from branch release/quickstart by 2026-03-15.
- Beta invite to early access group (internal + 10 customers) for two weeks.
- Collect metrics: time_to_first_token, failure rate, net-new tickets from beta cohort.
- GA if failure rate < 2% and onboarding time median < 7 minutes.

Notes to self / TODOs (short)
- [ ] finalize telemetry schema (owner: Sofia) RDW-1024
- [ ] add Windows-specific note for setting env vars (owner: Omar)
- [ ] add Dockerfile for sample app (owner: Liam)
- [ ] write 2-line troubleshooting copy for missing CAs / corporate proxies
- [ ] record 2 short screencasts (install + first-run)

Clip: quick failure-mode blurbs for README troubleshooting
- "No API key or unauthorized": error shows clear instructions to find API key in Console -> API keys.
- "Stuck at Connecting / no tokens": suggest check network, proxy, and set REDWOOD_REGION explicitly.
- "Streaming slow or empty": enable debug logs (REDWOOD_DEBUG=1) and open a support ticket with request_id.

Reference notes (internal)
- Keep SDK repo tidy: examples/quickstart should be single-file minimal app and full-sample with tests.
- CI artifact: publish sample zip to releases/tagged-beta and point README to that URL.

Open: review by content + legal for public copy by 2026-03-09.

---
Notes: this is intentionally concise and rough. Use this as the single-source working log for the quickstart sprint; move finalized text out to /docs/quickstart when copy is approved.
